newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy ends mixed, nearbys up on exports, wheat.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy ends mixed, nearbys up on exports, wheat.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed mixed with nearby contracts higher on strong weekly USDA export inspections data and on spillover support from wheat, traders said.

Trade was choppy most of the day amid conflicting weather reports. Some traders cited forecasts for rains this week in key Brazilian soybean growing regions while others subscribed to predictions for hot, dry conditions.
Independent meteorologist Somar predicted rain in key soybean growing regions of Rio Grande do Sul, Parana and Santa Catarina at the end of this week.
But the Brazilian forecaster added rainfall would be scattered with lower accumulations than last weekend's storm.

Nearby months drew strength from USDA's weekly export inspections data which pegged soybean export inspections for the week ended January 16 at 35.3 million bushels, above the highest trade estimate of 27.0 million bushels.
But some traders noted the inspections tally offset last week's disappointing number of 22.2 million bushels.
Soybeans closed 1-3/4 cents per bushel higher to 3/4 cent lower with March up 1/2 at $7.46-3/4.
Commercials were on both sides of the market. However, ADM, Produce Grain and Cargill Inc were all said to be net buyers on the day.
Refco Inc reportedly bought 1.0 million bushels March but sold 1.5 million March and 1.0 million May, traders said.
In options, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer reportedly bought 600 May $7.50 calls and sold 600 March $7.50 calls.
